questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect your ability to ride?

options.text: After about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired well before reaching the legal alcohol limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: Which item does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From someone who knows about motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It contains details about how to operate your bike and how to maintain it.

questions.question: What must you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can exceed the speed limit to complete the pass.
You can ignore no-passing zone markings if you started in a passing zone.
You can pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and only pass where it is legal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and only pass where it is legal.
questions.explanation: Complete all passes within posted speed limits. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: For best protection, what should your jacket and pants do?

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should cover all of your arms and legs. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials give the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Is a helmet required?

options.text: Only if the rider is under 18.
Only if the operator has had their license for two years or less.

questions.explanation: In Vermont, all motorcycle riders and passengers must wear helmets. A DOT-approved helmet is the best protection against serious injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see far to the sides for safe riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see far to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your side vision. You will be able to see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a vehicle's blind spot?

options.text: Stay in that position to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down to get out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to leave that area.

questions.question: What should you check about your brakes before riding?

options.text: They make a loud squeaking noise.
They cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake separately before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and can hold your motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: What should you do when stopped behind another vehicle?

options.text: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Do not use your rearview mirrors.
Look for ways to squeeze through the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle approaches too quickly from behind.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Pre-ride checks only by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. You must check your motorcycle more often. Do a full check before every ride.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day.

questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials to be more visible, especially at night. Bright clothing with reflective materials helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, you should look at all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check the air pressure, tread, and general wear of your tires. How shiny a tire is does not matter.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active substance in marijuana is THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Road rule signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let a tailgater pass when you can. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, oil, and metal plates are all slippery. Dry pavement provides the best grip.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Usually does not change how a motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for new riders.
Can change how a motorcycle handles.
Is encouraged to help riders get used to different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can change how a motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to a motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on your motorcycle's handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: If you must cross a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: When crossing a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off other vehicles.
The one where other drivers can see you.
The one in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one where other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and helps them see you. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good position discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What should you check before riding?

options.text: How much padding your seat has

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.
